questions.question: Where do four-magnon interactions come from in spin-wave theory?

options.b: from the quartic terms of the Holstein–Primakoff expansion (n_i n_j and the a†aa corrections of S±)

questions.explanation: S⁺ = √2S (a − a†aa/4S) and Sᶻ = S − n produce quartic boson terms on every bond.

questions.question: What does the Hartree–Fock (Wick) decoupling do?

options.b: replaces O1O2O3O4 by Σ_pairings ⟨O_aO_b⟩ O_cO_d — a renormalised quadratic Hamiltonian

questions.explanation: With thermal correlations ⟨a†a⟩, ⟨aa⟩ from the spin-wave spectrum.

questions.question: Hands-on: FM chain (S = 1.5, J = −5 meV) at T = 0: HF − LSWT magnon energy at k = 1 Å⁻¹ (meV)?
questions.explanation: The fully polarised ferromagnet is an exact eigenstate: no zero-point correction.

questions.question: Hands-on: same chain at T = 200 K, first-order HF energy at k = 1 Å⁻¹ (meV, 2 decimals)?
questions.explanation: 19.57 meV vs 30.75 meV in LSWT — Dyson's thermal softening, reproduced exactly.

questions.question: Hands-on: AFM chain, S = 1/2: renormalisation factor Z = ω_HF/ω_LSWT (4 decimals)?
Hands-on: square-lattice AFM, S = 1/2: Z (3 decimals)?
questions.explanation: Oguchi's spin-wave velocity renormalisation Z_c = 1 + 0.158/(2S).

questions.question: Physically, the Oguchi factor Z_c > 1 means …

options.b: zero-point (quantum) fluctuations reduce the ordered moment but stiffen the spin waves

questions.explanation: Bond correlations ⟨a_ia_j⟩ from zero-point motion renormalise the exchange upwards by r/2S.

questions.question: Hands-on: what happens to ⟨S^z⟩ of the S = 1/2 AFM chain as the k grid is refined?

options.b: it decreases without bound (logarithmic divergence): no long-range order in 1D

questions.explanation: ∫dk/|k| diverges in 1D: spin-wave theory signals the absence of Néel order.

questions.question: Hands-on: FM chain at T = 100 K, SELF-CONSISTENT HF energy at k = 1 Å⁻¹ (meV, 2 decimals)?
questions.explanation: 26.25 meV (first order: 27.28 meV): self-consistency enhances the softening.

questions.question: Hands-on: self-consistent HF for the FM chain at 200 K …

options.b: has no solution — the spin-wave Hamiltonian becomes unstable (no 1D order at T > 0)

questions.explanation: SymPhase stops with an explanatory error (Mermin–Wagner physics).

questions.question: For which magnets is the HF result the complete 1/S correction?

options.b: collinear magnets; non-collinear orders also have cubic terms of the same order (not included)

questions.explanation: Cubic terms contribute at second order with the same power of 1/S in non-collinear structures.

questions.question: How is the self-energy related to the golden-rule linewidth γ?

options.b: γ = −2 Im Σ(ω0) (exactly, with the same broadening)

questions.explanation: Checked to 10⁻¹² in the tests; Re Σ and the ω-dependence are new information.

questions.question: Hands-on: −2 Im Σ of the longitudinal phonon at q = 0.9 Å⁻¹ (dJ/dr = 1, T = 300 K, η = 0.05, grid 600) in meV (4 decimals)?
questions.explanation: ≈ 0.0185 meV, identical to the Lorentzian golden rule.

questions.question: Hands-on: Re Σ of the zone-boundary magnon (dJ/dr = 1 meV/Å, 300 K) in meV (3 decimals)?
questions.explanation: −0.044 meV: a small downward shift; the spectral peak moves to ≈ 20.57 meV.

questions.question: Hands-on: dJ/dr = 3 meV/Å — where is the spectral peak of the zone-boundary magnon (bare 20.6 meV)?

options.b: at ≈ 23.17 meV: a split-off state above the phonon-emission continuum edge

questions.explanation: Re Σ diverges at the 1D continuum edge (22.85 meV); a sharp state forms above it.

questions.question: Hands-on: spectral weight within ±1 meV of that split-off peak (2 decimals)?
questions.explanation: ≈ 0.22: most of the weight is smeared over the continuum — far from a Lorentzian quasiparticle.

questions.question: What does the sum rule ∫A(ω)dω = 1 check?

options.b: the analytic structure (causality, normalisation) of the self-energy and the ω window

questions.explanation: It holds to ≈ 2×10⁻⁴ for the 1D magnon spectral function.

questions.question: Why are the 'anti-resonant' (all-creation / all-annihilation) terms kept?

options.b: they contribute to Re Σ (energy shift) although they never conserve energy

questions.explanation: Their poles lie at negative ω, so they only shift the energy.

questions.question: Which CLI options compute the four-magnon renormalisation?
questions.explanation: Writes *_hf.png/.dat with LSWT and HF bands.

questions.question: Which CLI option draws the magnon spectral function from the magnon–phonon self-energy?
questions.explanation: Writes *_spectral.png (log A(k, ω) along the path).
